dataset: Stieger et al. 2021, continuous cursor-control BCI (figshare 13123148)

rest.note: The input leads outside the default subset, same rate, unit and filters, in time chunks per segment (channel-major within a chunk).

window_note: The display runs from 2 s before the target appears to 4 s after it. The model reads the 4 s after the target appears (lighter band): 2 s with the target on screen, then the first 2 s of cursor control.
time_axis_note: The session file stores one array per trial with its own time vector (ms from the appearance of the target: 2 s pause, 2 s target, cursor control until the result, 1 s after it) and no clock time between trials. The time axis here is the concatenation of the trial arrays in file order, the same axis the benchmark split lists use; it is not wall-clock time. Runs are shown as separate segments because the file does not record the time between them.
display_conversion: session file in µV, trials concatenated on the session time axis, 0.5 Hz zero-phase FIR high-pass, polyphase resampling 1000 Hz to 200 Hz; the model input is the same band at 200 Hz for the 4 s after the target appears, standardised per recording and lead and clipped at ±15 SD. The replay holds all 60 leads the model reads; 13 are shown by default

provenance.selection_note: Development (validation) split. Participant with the highest top-answer accuracy among the 13 development participants (0.765 over 2,091 trials), and that participant’s session with the highest accuracy (0.864 over 177 retained trials). Within the session: the run of 24 consecutive retained trials that contains all four options and has the most correct top answers. The replay shows every trial of the file between the first and the last of them, including trials that are not in the benchmark split (those have no saved answer).
